question: Will under 58% of the contiguous U.S. be in drought on October 27, 2026?

calls.reasoning: USDM CONUS D1-D4 was 55.21% on the Oct 6 map, down 4.2 pts from 59.38% on Sep 29 after a large early-October rain event. The question needs <58% on the Oct 27 map, so a rise of more than 2.8 pts in 3 weeks would be needed for NO. Summer 2026 shows such rises can happen (48.5 to 56.6 in Aug, up to 59.4 in Sep), but the current direction is improvement: more rain mid-Oct (Missouri), and the 6-10 day outlook leans near/above-normal precipitation for most of the country. The risk comes from dry Plains, the western Corn Belt and the Pacific NW. No market found on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold.

calls.reasoning: Latest USDM CONUS D1-D4 (Oct 6 map) is 55.21%, 2.79 pts below the 58% threshold, with three weekly maps left. Using Jun-Oct 2026 weekly volatility (most weeks within ±2.5), a neutral-drift 3-week rise of more than 2.8 pts is roughly 15-20% likely. Heavy rain forecast for TX/OK/KS/MO on Oct 14-16, a wet CPC 6-10 day outlook and a monthly drought outlook favouring improvement tilt the drift down. Against that, the dry Oct 7-13 week in the southern Plains/mid-South may push the Oct 13 map up 1-2 pts, and the Midwest and Pacific NW could worsen. No human market found.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on the factual baseline: 55.21% on Oct 6, 59.38% on Sep 29, and an August rise of about 8 pts showing large moves are possible. The one factual dispute is how the Oct 13 map moves after a dry Oct 7-13 week in the southern Plains/mid-South. Run 3 expects a 1-2 pt worsening. I could not settle this without the map, so I keep it as uncertainty. The heavy rain forecast for Oct 14-16 is not in dispute and would show up on the Oct 20 map. The rest is judgment about drift. Forecast rain and the CPC outlooks lean toward improvement, the Drought Monitor usually keeps lifting categories for weeks after a big rain, and the risk of Midwest and Pacific NW worsening plus the likely Oct 13 rise lean the other way. Against 2.8 pts of headroom and ~3.5 pts of 3-week volatility, that lands me at about 0.84.
